_readme: Persistent, structured record of what's actually known about this car's CAN traffic -- the reusable output of every reverse-engineering session, instead of re-deriving context from prose docs each time.

This file is read by tools/can_id_triage.py to filter already-known IDs out of its ranked 'worth investigating' report. It is NOT written automatically by that script -- entries are added/edited by hand (or by Claude on request) only once a finding is actually confirmed, to avoid polluting it with unverified guesses.
id keys are uppercase hex with a 0x prefix, e.g. "0x7E8". Use the shortest form for the addressing scheme actually used (11-bit standard vs 29-bit extended) -- don't zero-pad.
kind: one of uds_diagnostic | obd_request | obd_response | broadcast_decoded | broadcast_undecoded | unknown
confidence: one of confirmed | candidate | present_confirmed (id/payload seen and stable, but meaning not decoded) | unconfirmed

signals: list of {name, byte_offset, length, endian, scale, offset, unit, notes} for anything actually decoded at the byte level. Leave empty ([]) until something is confirmed -- most entries below are intentionally signal-less right now.

0x7DF.label: OBD-II Mode 01 functional request (standard 11-bit)
0x7DF.notes: This car answers on the classic 0x7DF/0x7E8-0x7EF range, not 29-bit extended, despite other bus traffic (0x17F00010, 0x1BFC8202) using 29-bit IDs.

0x7E8.label: Engine ECU (OBD Mode 01/09 response)
0x7E8.notes: Real engine ECU -- richer PID support (17 PIDs page 1: 01,03,04,05,06,07,0B,0C,0D,0E,0F,11,13,15,1C,1F,20; 9 PIDs page 2: 21,2E,2F,30,31,33,34,3C,40). RPM/speed/throttle live-confirmed tracking real acceleration. VIN (Mode 09 PID 02) confirmed: TMBER9PJ3T4015474. Decode formulas are standard OBD Mode 01 (see main.c obd_print_response), not raw fixed-offset broadcast signals, so not itemized in 'signals' below.

0x7E9.label: Secondary/gateway module (OBD Mode 01 response, mirrors a subset of engine signals)
0x7E9.notes: Narrower PID support (7 PIDs page 1: 01,04,05,0C,0D,0F,20; 2 PIDs page 2: 33,40). Values track 0x7E8's within 1-3%, not stale/frozen. Responder-lock in obd_query_task picks 0x7E8 first and ignores this one for the rest of a PID sequence.

0x710.label: Gateway (UDS diagnostic)
0x710.notes: Only address that responds across a full 0x700-0x7FF UDS sweep. Identifies itself as supplier 'Har', part '3Q0'. Not a broadcast signal source -- point-to-point diagnostic only.

0x77A.label: Gateway UDS response (see 0x710)
0x77A.notes: The Gateway's own response id, captured passively during the 2026-09-15 address-scan session. Not a separate module -- same node as 0x710.

0x70D.label: Central Convenience / Comfort System -- candidate body module (unreachable via direct UDS)
0x70D.notes: Response id 0x777. Times out on direct 0x10/0x22 UDS requests. Unconfirmed whether it broadcasts unprompted -- check via passive capture before assuming fully unreachable.

0x71E.notes: Response id 0x788. Times out on direct 0x10/0x22 UDS requests.

0x74A.notes: Response id 0x7B4. Times out on direct 0x10/0x22 UDS requests.

0x74B.notes: Response id 0x7B5. Times out on direct 0x10/0x22 UDS requests.

0x73E.label: Rear Driver Door -- candidate body module (untested)
0x73E.notes: Response id 0x7A8. Lower priority than the others -- not yet UDS-tested at all per UDS_BODY_MODULE_RESEARCH.md.

0x714.notes: Response id 0x77E. Listed for cross-reference, not actively pursued.

0x78F.label: Closed dead lead -- do not re-pursue
0x78F.notes: Response id 0x7F9 replied '7F 10 31' (negative response to Diagnostic Session Control -- 'service not supported'). Investigated and closed; removed from UdsTargets.java. Kept here so it isn't rediscovered and re-investigated from scratch.

0x17F00010.label: Dominant comfort/body heartbeat broadcast (29-bit extended, undecoded)
0x17F00010.notes: Present continuously, including with the car fully off and doors closed -- not tied to any specific triggered action (lock/unlock/door/headlights all showed only this ID in early Learn-wizard captures, before Active-mode testing ruled it out as the signal for any of them). Real rate ~2Hz in Active mode (Passive/Listen-Only mode falsely inflates it to ~730-750Hz via CAN auto-retransmit-on-no-ACK -- always analyze Active-mode captures for rate, never Passive). Payload is not fixed across sessions (seen: 20020000852A05D6, 2000000000000780). Treat as background noise and filter out of ID-triage ranking; a real signal (if one exists) for lock/unlock/etc. is more likely elsewhere or in a longer capture.

0x1BFC8202.label: Secondary background broadcast (29-bit extended, undecoded)
0x1BFC8202.notes: ~6.17s period. Payload seen: 8800000D00000000. Only visible in Active mode -- was being crowded out of the MCP2515's 2-deep hardware RX buffer by the 0x17F00010 no-ACK retransmit storm in Passive mode, never appeared in any Passive capture. Undecoded; filter out of ID-triage ranking alongside 0x17F00010 unless byte-liveness analysis finds something worth a closer look.
